facts.text: I have a large lump in my left armpit.

facts.item: lump in the left armpit: tenderness
facts.text: It's tender now.

facts.item: lump in the left armpit: onset
facts.text: I first noticed it 3 years ago, as a small lump that wasn't tender.

facts.item: lump in the left armpit: what was happening when it appeared
facts.text: That was 6 months after my contraceptive implant was put into my left arm, 8 months after my last baby was born, and 2 years after I arrived in the United States.

facts.item: lump in the left armpit: early growth
facts.text: At first it grew slowly and didn't hurt.

facts.item: lump in the left armpit: recent rapid growth
facts.text: Six months ago it started growing quickly and became tender.
While it was growing slowly, it never drained anything.

facts.item: skin changes over the lump while it grew slowly
facts.text: While it was growing slowly, the skin over it didn't change.
While it was growing slowly, it didn't cause any nerve symptoms.

facts.item: trouble breastfeeding because of the lump
facts.text: It didn't get in the way of breastfeeding.

facts.item: trouble bringing the left arm in to the side
facts.text: It stops me from bringing my left arm all the way in against my side.

facts.item: lump in the left armpit: discomfort when moving the arm
facts.text: It's mildly uncomfortable when I bring my arm in against my side.

facts.item: streaks on the skin over the lump
facts.text: Now there are stretch-mark-like streaks on the skin over it.
I haven't had any problems with my breasts.

aliases: injury to the arm or armpit
facts.text: I haven't had any injury.
I haven't had any infection.
I haven't had any general symptoms.
I haven't had any other exposures that I know of.
My only medication is a contraceptive implant, etonogestrel, in my left arm.
The implant was replaced 2 months before the lump started growing quickly.
I've had three full-term pregnancies.
I'm African; I immigrated to the United States from East Africa.

findings.name: examination of the left axilla
findings.result: Softball-sized, mobile, nonreducible mass in the left axillary fossa with overlying skin striations; mild discomfort with arm adduction.

findings.name: neurovascular examination of the left arm
findings.result: Intact vascular, sensory, and motor function.

findings.name: MRI of the left axilla
findings.result: 16 × 11 × 11 cm multiloculated subcutaneous cystic lesion displacing but not invading adjacent structures, without intrathoracic communication or lymphadenopathy.

findings.name: MR lymphangiogram
findings.result: After subcutaneous contrast injection into the interdigital web spaces: no lymphatic communication with the mass, although lymphatic drainage led to nodes over the lesion.

findings.name: initial laboratory studies
findings.result: Unremarkable, without evidence of systemic infection.

gold.reasoning: 1. Hydatid cyst remained a concern given patient’s origin, as “hydatid cyst could not definitively be ruled out” and serology was equivocal (“IgG testing was performed with equivocal results, indicating possible but not definitive presence of Echinococcus”). 2. Simple cyst was considered but excluded because “imaging was not consistent with typical appearance of … simple cyst.” 3. Abscess was on the initial differential but ruled out since “imaging was not consistent with typical appearance of abscess.” 4. Cavernous hemangioma was considered but excluded because “imaging was not consistent with typical appearance of … cavernous hemangioma.”

f022: The prompt calls the immigration 'recent' but s002 places her arrival 2 years before a lump first noticed 3 years ago (about 5 years before presentation); the text gives no arrival date (see source_issues).

source_issues: 'Recent immigration from East Africa' (s001) conflicts with s002, which places her arrival in the United States about 5 years before presentation.
The presenting mass is called tender (s001) while the examination reports only mild discomfort with arm adduction (s007).
notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation with the large, tender left axillary mass (s001–s008), with the imaging and serology of that evaluation (s009–s011).
The prior MRI (s009) is a finding with time 'before presentation'; the patient is not said to have been told its result.
Breastfeeding is not a separate fact: the source only says the lump did not interfere with it (f010).
Earlier timeline in f004 is kept relative ('6 months after the implant ...') as in the source, without computing dates.
